general.q: Which country hosted and won the inaugural FIFA Men's World Cup in 1930?
general.why: Uruguay defeated neighbouring Argentina 4–2 in the final in Montevideo.

general.q: The apple brandy Calvados is traditionally produced in which region of France?
general.why: Calvados has held Protected Designation of Origin status in Normandy since 1942.

general.q: Which country is the largest landlocked nation in the world by total land area?
general.why: Kazakhstan spans over 2.7 million square kilometres without an ocean coastline.

general.q: Which British monarch was the first to take up official residence at Buckingham Palace?
general.why: Victoria moved into the palace in July 1837, shortly after ascending the throne.

general.q: Which is the only living species of bear native to South America?
general.why: Also called the Andean bear, it gets its name from distinct markings around its eyes.

pop.q: In the Channel 4 sitcom Black Books, which comedian plays the bookshop's eccentric assistant Manny Bianco?
pop.why: Bill Bailey starred as Manny alongside Dylan Moran's misanthropic bookshop owner Bernard Black.

pop.q: Which miniature toy vehicle brand was famously advertised in the 1980s and 90s by fast-talking John Moschitta Jr.?
pop.why: Moschitta delivered the trademark rapid-fire slogan: "If it doesn't say Micro Machines, it's not the real thing!"

pop.q: In the 1998 game Metal Gear Solid, which boss famously breaks the fourth wall by reading the player's memory card?
pop.why: Psycho Mantis spooked players by commenting on save files from other Konami games and making the controller vibrate.

pop.q: In a classic 1980s Hamlet cigar advert, which Scottish actor struggles comically to take a passport photo in a booth?
pop.why: The Rab C. Nesbitt star's photo booth mishap remains one of British television's most celebrated adverts.

pop.q: On the comedy panel show Shooting Stars, which comedian played the scorekeeping giant baby George Dawes?
pop.why: Matt Lucas delivered scores from his drum kit and famously performed surreal tunes like the Baked Potato Song.

music.q: Which novelty act kept Take That's 'Babe' off the UK Christmas Number 1 spot in 1993?
music.why: Mr Blobby's self-titled single reached the top spot just in time for Christmas Day in 1993.

music.q: Which Oasis song did Jay-Z open his 2008 Glastonbury headline set with, mocking critics of hip-hop at the festival?
music.why: Jay-Z walked out with a guitar to cover Wonderwall after Noel Gallagher had questioned hip-hop headlining Glastonbury.

music.q: What was the title of rock band The Darkness's multi-platinum debut studio album, released in 2003?
music.why: Featuring 'I Believe in a Thing Called Love', Permission to Land topped the UK Albums Chart in 2003.

music.q: Which pop duo represented the UK at the 2003 Eurovision Song Contest, infamously scoring 'nul points'?
music.why: Jemini's rendition of 'Cry Baby' in Riga earned the UK its first ever zero-point Eurovision finish.

music.q: Which singer joined hip-hop group The Black Eyed Peas in 2002 ahead of their breakout album 'Elephunk'?
music.why: Fergie joined the existing trio in 2002, helping propel the group to global multi-platinum success.

mix.q: Which English indie rock band reached number one on the UK singles chart in 2007 with the hit 'Ruby'?
mix.why: Ruby was the lead single from Kaiser Chiefs' second studio album, Yours Truly, Angry Mob.

mix.q: In the BBC sitcom 'Gimme Gimme Gimme', what is the name of Linda's actor flatmate played by James Dreyfus?
mix.why: James Dreyfus played the flamboyant, struggling actor Tom Farrell alongside Kathy Burke's Linda.

mix.q: Which chemical element is the only metal that is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure?
mix.why: Mercury, also known as quicksilver, has a melting point of minus 38.8 degrees Celsius.

mix.q: Which mountain peak is the highest point in Wales and the entire British Isles outside Scotland?
mix.why: Standing at 1,085 metres, Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) is the highest peak in Wales.

mix.q: In the 2004 comedy horror film 'Shaun of the Dead', what is the name of the pub where the heroes take shelter?
mix.why: Shaun famously decides to head to The Winchester, have a nice cold pint, and wait for it all to blow over.

mix.q: Which classic dessert consists of a dark, dense sponge containing chopped dates, smothered in a toffee sauce?
mix.why: Sticky toffee pudding was originally developed in the mid-20th century in North West England.

mix.q: In the PlayStation video game series 'Crash Bandicoot', what is the name of Crash's main arch-nemesis?
mix.why: Doctor Neo Cortex is the yellow-skinned mad scientist determined to dominate the world.

mix.q: Which English monarch succeeded King Henry VIII upon his death in 1547?
mix.why: Edward VI became king at just nine years old and was the son of Henry VIII and Jane Seymour.

mix.q: Who served as Lord Sugar's original male advisor alongside Margaret Mountford on BBC's 'The Apprentice'?
mix.why: Nick Hewer advised Lord Sugar for ten series before leaving the show in 2014.

mix.q: Which American hard rock band released the landmark 1987 debut album 'Appetite for Destruction'?
mix.why: Appetite for Destruction became one of the best-selling debut albums of all time.
